A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SeeGround, with matching authors, methods, and core experiments. The complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, support reliable comparison despite reflow and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original ScanRefer and Nr3D grounding results, component ablations, error analysis, and appendix experiments comparing VLMs and visual prompts.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a ScanRefer study comparing detector choices and ground-truth proposals in Appendix Section 7.3.

M1.justification: The hybrid scene representation, Perspective Adaptation Module, Fusion Alignment Module, and object-ID prediction procedure are retained. The added detector study tests alternative configurations of the existing framework rather than introducing a new algorithm component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ScanRefer and Nr3D grounding tasks. Alternative detectors, ground-truth proposals, and the added comparator's smaller sample set change experimental settings without establishing new dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds VLM-Grounder to the ScanRefer comparison in Table 1 and MiKASA and ViL3DRel to the Nr3D comparison in Table 2. Existing comparators remain, making this a limited expansion of baseline coverage.

E3.justification: New Table 10 evaluates OVIR-3D and ground-truth proposals alongside the retained Mask3D setting. The added VLM-Grounder row explicitly uses 250 selected ScanRefer samples. Existing rendering resolution, scene cropping, VLM choice, and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix Section 7.3 and Table 10 add a focused analysis of sensitivity to detector choice and performance with ground-truth proposals. Existing architecture, viewpoint, language-agent, visual-prompt, and error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the grounding results. The existing random-sampling descriptions for supplementary analyses are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds VLM-Grounder's ScanRefer results of 51.6/32.8 at Acc@0.25/0.5 on 250 samples and Nr3D results of 64.4 for both MiKASA and ViL3DRel. Table 10 adds OVIR-3D accuracies of 30.7/19.3 for SeeGround/ZSVG3D and 59.5 for SeeGround with ground-truth proposals. Existing results are retained; these are additional entries, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–17, including the camera-transform derivations and point/object visibility definitions in the appendix, retain their mathematical content. Changes concern notation and typesetting; no new assumptions, proofs, or formal results appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the training-free grounding framework, its two modules, and its performance claims. The headline improvements of 7.7% on ScanRefer and 7.1% on Nr3D remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7.3 newly interprets ground-truth-proposal performance as an upper bound and discusses improvement potential from better detection. v1 already warned about detection-error propagation; the existing limitations concerning rendering, clutter, small objects, and dynamic scenes remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies Mask3D behind the retained ScanRefer detection setting, which v1 described through a reference to ZSVG3D's procedure. It also describes the existing project website as providing demo and code, without establishing when these became available. Existing prompts and rendering details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for the new comparators and Mask3D, brief coverage of PQ3D and Glover, and broader application references. The related-work categories and central positioning around visual information versus text-driven grounding remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language edits throughout the abstract, introduction, and method description, converts the numbered Overview subsection into introductory prose, and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 expands Tables 1 and 2, adds Table 10, and updates captions and score emphasis. Existing figures and appendix tables are retained but repositioned, including moving the extended qualitative figure after the limitations and resource sections. The visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The detector study supplies empirical evidence for a dependency that v1 discussed mainly qualitatively, while additional baselines broaden the comparison. These are useful, limited improvements. VLM-Grounder's unmatched 250-sample setting and Table 10's unspecified accuracy threshold constrain the strength of the added evidence.
